subject: Order Form: prepay / staircase commit schedule, VAT treatment and payment carveouts
messages:
From: Sasha Venkataraman <sasha@citrine.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Leonard Price <l.price@citrine.com>, procurement@citrine.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: prepay / staircase commit schedule, VAT treatment and payment carveouts

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. We reviewed the order form and have two open items from procurement and legal that block signature:

1) VAT handling for EU entities: our tax team needs clarity whether Redwood will invoice gross (adding VAT) versus issuing net invoices under reverse-charge when we provide a valid VAT number. We attached our VAT certificate for review.

2) Prepay / staircase schedule: we prefer a two-tranche prepay (50% upfront, 50% at month 6) for the 12-month minimum commit. The current draft assumes full prepay; can Redwood support tranche billing and a smaller prepay on signature? We are prepared to accept a small premium for staged prepay.

Also a short ask on payment terms: Citrine typically pushes Net 60 on enterprise contracts. Is there flexibility to move Net 30 on the prepay portion and Net 60 on the remainder?

We attached a redline PDF with suggested edits (high level). Can you confirm who at Redwood will own the VAT evidence flow and whether your finance team needs anything else from us?

Thanks,
Sasha Venkataraman
Head of Procurement
Citrine Labs

[Attachment: Citrine_VAT_certificate.pdf (PDF, 12KB)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Venkataraman <sasha@citrine.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: prepay / staircase commit schedule, VAT treatment and payment carveouts

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear asks and for sending the VAT cert. High level answers below; going to loop in finance and legal for the exact contract language and to confirm DocuSign flow.

VAT treatment:
- Redwood can support net invoicing under reverse-charge provided Citrine supplies a valid EU VAT ID and completes our VAT evidence form within 30 days of signature. If evidence arrives later than 30 days we will need to re-issue adjusted invoices which can delay accounting.
- Internal: Kimberly, please confirm the recommended MSA clause and whether 30 days is acceptable. Also confirm evidence collection mechanism (we typically collect via secure Drive link and store hash in the invoice meta).

Prepay / staircase:
- We can accept a two-tranche prepay for this customer: 50% at signature, 50% at month 6. Standard pricing uplift for staged prepay is +3% overall (reflects credit exposure).
- We need to map this to the billing schedule and order form: tranche 1 will be invoiced on signature (Net 30), tranche 2 invoiced on the calendar date six months after signature (Net 30). Remaining monthly consumption billed monthly in arrears.

Payment terms carveout:
- We can make an exception to split Net 30 on prepay tranches and Net 60 on consumption invoices if procurement signs off; would need finance approval to accept Net 60 on recurring items.

Next steps:
- Kimberly / Ben: see attached redline from Citrine. Can Legal propose contract mark (MSA section 5.x VAT; Order Form section 2.1 prepay schedule) and confirm whether the 30-day evidence window and +3% uplift are OK operationally?
- Sasha: I’ll upload a draft DocuSign packet with the revised prepay schedule once we get legal approval.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment referenced: Citrine_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form: prepay / staircase commit schedule, VAT treatment and payment carveouts

Thanks for the tag, Grace. Quick take from legal and tax: 

1) VAT language: propose the following insertion to the MSA (new subclause):
"Customer shall be responsible for VAT, sales, use or other indirect taxes, except where Customer provides a valid EU VAT registration number and supporting documentation within thirty (30) days of signature, in which case Redwood will issue invoices net of VAT and Customer agrees to self-account under the reverse-charge mechanism. If valid documentation is not provided within the thirty (30) day window, invoices will be reissued with VAT and applicable taxes will be due."

This mirrors our current language but explicitly states the 30-day evidence window and re-issue process.

2) Prepay / staircase: Legal is comfortable with a two-tranche prepay but requests the following: a clear payment schedule table on the Order Form, a clause that ties the second tranche invoicing to a fixed calendar date (e.g., 6 months from signature) and an explicit non-refundable designation for the prepay tranches (unless otherwise agreed). Also note operationally: Finance will apply a +3% uplift to the effective price for staged prepay.

3) Net terms carveout: Finance says Net 30 on tranches; Net 60 acceptable on consumption only if procurement signs written acceptance and we add a late-payment interest clause (0.5% per month) to protect cash flow.

Action items (I’ll own legal redline):
- I will prepare a short amendment paragraph for the MSA (VAT) and a replacement Order Form table with the tranche rows and the non-refundable label.
- Ben / Finance: please confirm the exact wording for the +3% uplift and the late-interest clause so I can add it.

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: draft-msav1-vat-clause.docx (referred to for redline)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Order Form: prepay / staircase commit schedule, VAT treatment and payment carveouts

Acknowledged — finance confirms the +3% uplift on staircase prepay and proposes this line for the Order Form appendix: 
"Staircase Prepay Adjustment: A 3% prepay uplift is applied to the effective unit price when the customer elects a staged prepayment schedule (50% at signature, 50% at six months). Prepay tranches are non-refundable and will be invoiced as follows: Tranche 1 — on signature (Net 30); Tranche 2 — six (6) months from signature (Net 30). Consumption invoices follow the standard monthly arrears cadence (Net 60 as agreed)."

Also proposing this finance-friendly payment assurance clause to add to the Order Form: 
"If Customer fails to provide valid VAT evidence within thirty (30) days and has already benefited from net invoicing, Redwood reserves the right to reissue prior invoices to include VAT and to withhold service until outstanding tax liabilities are resolved."

Happy to prep the invoice schedule table for the Order Form template.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
